blocked_on: Approval to install a CPU tensor library (e.g. torch CPU or numpy+autograd). Training in pure Python is not feasible at this size.
Approval of the CPU budget below.
decision_question: In a trained, multi-layer selective SSM, does simple time handling (Delta = dt*g, exact ZOH B, time-weighted readout) or resampling onto a fixed time grid with the SAME backbone remove the grid artifact of the Mamba-style recipe? If yes, the new-architecture claim is dropped for good.
why_this_is_the_decision_experiment: FIRST_RUN showed that in a single fixed-parameter layer the simple fix removes the splitting artifact to float64 precision (stop condition S2 triggered at toy level). TIDES (arXiv 2605.09742) already occupies the architecture of physical Delta + exact ZOH + selectivity on Lambda. The only remaining question that could matter is whether residual artifacts (conv1d over tokens, inter-layer hold in deep stacks, learned gates evaluated at new samples) survive the simple fixes in trained models.

data.source: synthetic, generated in-repo from integer seeds; no external data
teachers: T1: the FIRST_RUN continuous-time selective system with fixed teacher parameters (favours ZOH-type students; reported separately)
T2: a nonlinear system not in any student class (e.g. forced damped Duffing oscillator), to avoid a teacher-student match
data.split: split trajectory IDs FIRST into train/dev/test = 512/128/256; only THEN build grids for each split independently; no trajectory appears in two splits in any grid form
data.train_grids: one base density (K=16 on [0,8]) with jitter; optional second arm trained on mixed densities, reported separately
test_grids: pure splitting m in {1,2,4,8} (held values repeated)

stem: linear interpolation of the observations (exact first-order-hold integration)
exact ZOH of the held observations
backbone: fixed time grid (uniform delta_fixed, independent of observations)

required_baselines: S5: MIMO LTI, exact ZOH with per-step dt (strongest direct LTI baseline)
S4D-ZOH (LTI) on the fixed time grid after resampling
resampling onto the fixed grid + the SAME selective backbone (simplest alternative)
Mamba-style recipe on the observed grid: Delta = softplus(.), Euler B, depthwise conv1d k=4, no dt (grid-dependent reference)
Mamba-style + dt appended as an input channel (S5-append analogue)
simple-fix selective: Delta = dt*g, exact ZOH B, time-weighted readout, conv1d removed or replaced by a time-indexed kernel
TIDES-like: physical Delta, selectivity on Re(Lambda), B, C (closest prior work)

metrics.primary_consistency: rel_l2 of outputs at common times under pure splitting, m=8 vs m=1, per test trajectory
metrics.primary_accuracy: rel_l2 to the continuous-time teacher at the training density, per test trajectory
secondary: error to teacher under new observations, m in {2,4,8}
time-average readout error under density change
per-component ablation: conv1d on/off, readout sample-mean vs time-exact
metrics.aggregation: mean over test trajectories with a bootstrap 95% CI over trajectories; 3 training seeds reported separately (seeds are not independent data units)
metrics.numerical_floor: float32 composition drift measured in FR-E4-N4 (emulated): about 1e-7 to 1e-4 relative for 16 to 16384 sub-steps; consistency differences below 1e-4 are treated as numerically indistinguishable in float32

budget.hyperparameters: one shared setting per model family; learning rate chosen on dev from at most 3 values, the same grid for every model; no further sweep

hypotheses_draft.NX1-H1: The Mamba-style recipe on the observed grid has splitting inconsistency >= 1e-1 at m=8 (toy analogue: FR-E1 eulerB_nodt median 1.18).
hypotheses_draft.NX1-H2: The simple-fix selective model OR resampling + same backbone reaches splitting inconsistency <= 1e-3 at m=8 with primary accuracy no worse than the best baseline by more than 5% relative.
hypotheses_draft.NX1-H3 (CONJECTURE): With depth >= 2 on the observed grid, the simple-fix model keeps a residual O(dt) splitting inconsistency because the input of layer 2 becomes a finer held sampling of layer 1's continuous output; the fixed-time-grid backbone removes it.

stop_conditions.S-arch: If NX1-H2 holds for either simple fix, stop any new-architecture claim; at most an analysis note remains.
stop_conditions.S-null: If no model, including the Mamba-style recipe, shows splitting inconsistency above the float32 floor after training, stop the project question (the effect is not practically relevant in this setting).
